entities.summary:
General Electric Company (GE) is an American multinational conglomerate founded in 1892 through the merger of Edison General Electric and Thomson-Houston, incorporating Thomas Edison's electrical inventions. Once the most valuable company in the world and the only original Dow Jones Industrial Average member to remain on the index for over a century, GE defined American industrial capitalism.

GE's early decades commercialized Edison's electrical innovations, electrifying homes and factories across America. Under CEO Jack Welch (1981-2001), GE became the world's most valuable company and a management philosophy institution, pioneering Six Sigma quality management, forced ranking employee systems, and aggressive financial services expansion through GE Capital. Welch's management methods were widely emulated globally.

GE's subsequent decline under Jeff Immelt, marked by GE Capital's near-collapse in 2008, overextension into power and oil & gas, and $222 billion in shareholder value destruction, became a textbook case in conglomerate failure. GE announced in 2021 it would split into three separate companies: GE Aerospace, GE HealthCare (spun off 2023), and GE Vernova (energy, spun off 2024). The breakup closed the chapter on the 20th-century industrial conglomerate model.
